about: Every ISSPG compact variable sorted into input / optimisation / fixed / dependent. 'cad_variables' are the 145 variables ISSPG compact writes to CADs/ISSPG/isspg_compact_equations_onshape.txt, in that order (this gearbox has no other equation file); 'code_only' are values the code uses but does not write to the CAD file, plus every config key the CAD does not use; 'unused_config_blocks' are config blocks ISSPG never reads. tests/test_variable_categories.py checks the lists against the code and re-evaluates every formula and lookup; docs/variables/isspg_compact.md is generated from this file (python tools/variables/render.py).

categories.input: chosen parts and material: the motor's dimensions and torque, the motor driver's mount dimensions, the gear material's allowable stress
categories.optimisation: searched by the optimiser: teeth, module, number of planets
categories.fixed: constants that don't depend on the design: clearances, wall thicknesses, fastener and bearing choices, feature sizes, the gear standard
categories.dependent: computed from the variables above, by a formula, a catalogue lookup (bearings, bolts, nuts) or a rule the code applies (the tooth-stress rule for face widths)

confidence.high: the code reads it directly from one source, or computes it with an explicit formula
confidence.medium: the code is clear, but the category is a judgement call (see the reason)
confidence.low: can't be decided from the code alone

cad_variables.name: fw_s_calc
cad_variables.rule: b = FOS x Ft x qe x qk / (gear_allowable_stress x module) (mitStressAnalysisMinFacewidth), with Ft = serviceFactor x motor_peak_torque / (num_planet x sun pitch radius), qe = 1 / sun-planet contact ratio, qk = curve fit in Ns; if b < 2 x planet_bearing_width + planet_bearing_gap, the planet and ring width is raised to that value; then the gears must fit the stator height less gear_axial_margin_mm: when the ring is wider than that, all three widths are scaled by (stator_height - gear_axial_margin_mm) / ring width, so the capped gears carry the same fraction of the torque; fw_s_calc = b (scaled)
cad_variables.reason: sun face width from the tooth-stress rule, scaled by the stator-height cap when it applies: fixed by the optimisation variables, the motor torque, the gear material, the safety factors and the cap

cad_variables.name: alpha_s
cad_variables.formula: sqrt(dp_s ** 2 - db_s ** 2) / db_s * 180 / pi - pressure_angle_rad * 180 / pi
cad_variables.reason: involute angle used to draw the tooth

cad_variables.name: beta_s
cad_variables.reason: tooth angle used to draw the tooth

cad_variables.reason: pitch diameter

cad_variables.name: db_p
cad_variables.reason: base-circle diameter

cad_variables.name: fw_p
cad_variables.rule: b = FOS x Ft x qe x qk / (gear_allowable_stress x module) (mitStressAnalysisMinFacewidth), with Ft = serviceFactor x motor_peak_torque / (num_planet x sun pitch radius), qe = 1 / sun-planet contact ratio, qk = curve fit in Ns; if b < 2 x planet_bearing_width + planet_bearing_gap, the planet and ring width is raised to that value; then the gears must fit the stator height less gear_axial_margin_mm: when the ring is wider than that, all three widths are scaled by (stator_height - gear_axial_margin_mm) / ring width, so the capped gears carry the same fraction of the torque; fw_p = b (scaled)
cad_variables.reason: planet face width from the tooth-stress rule, raised to hold its two bearings and scaled by the stator-height cap (the ring width is the same value)

cad_variables.name: alpha_p
cad_variables.formula: sqrt(dp_p ** 2 - db_p ** 2) / db_p * 180 / pi - pressure_angle_rad * 180 / pi
cad_variables.reason: involute angle used to draw the tooth

cad_variables.reason: tooth angle used to draw the tooth

cad_variables.reason: ring face width from the tooth-stress rule, raised to the planet-bearing minimum and scaled by the stator-height cap (the planet width is the same value)

cad_variables.name: carrier_thickness_mid
cad_variables.formula: 6 if (fw_s_used + clearance_planet + (6 + carrier_thickness_top) - (motor_case_thickness - bearing_step_width) - motor_height) >= 3 else (motor_height + 3 + motor_case_thickness - bearing_step_width - fw_s_used - clearance_planet) - carrier_thickness_top
cad_variables.reason: middle carrier plate: a hard-coded 6 mm, or, when the ring hub would be thinner than a hard-coded 3 mm, what remains of the carrier after the top; an iterative two-case rule with two hard-coded numbers

cad_variables.name: carrier_thickness
cad_variables.formula: (6 + carrier_thickness_top) if (fw_s_used + clearance_planet + (6 + carrier_thickness_top) - (motor_case_thickness - bearing_step_width) - motor_height) >= 3 else (motor_height + 3 + motor_case_thickness - bearing_step_width - fw_s_used - clearance_planet)
cad_variables.reason: carrier thickness: the hard-coded 6 mm middle plate plus the top, or, when the ring hub would be thinner than a hard-coded 3 mm, whatever closes the stack; an iterative two-case rule with two hard-coded numbers

cad_variables.name: ring_hub_thickness
cad_variables.formula: (fw_s_used + clearance_planet + (6 + carrier_thickness_top) - (motor_case_thickness - bearing_step_width) - motor_height) if (fw_s_used + clearance_planet + (6 + carrier_thickness_top) - (motor_case_thickness - bearing_step_width) - motor_height) >= 3 else 3
cad_variables.reason: ring hub thickness: whatever lets the stack reach the motor, but at least a hard-coded 3 mm (the config's ring_hub_thickness is not read); an iterative two-case rule with two hard-coded numbers
